summary: Created appworker on node1 and configured all PAM-backed login sessions with soft and hard limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes. The account, limits, SSH access, and system health persisted across the required node restart.
actions_performed: Created appworker with /home/appworker, /bin/bash, and a locked password by default.
Verified exact limits in PAM login sessions and confirmed attempts to exceed either hard limit are denied.
Restarted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity and full recovery.
Confirmed RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, relevant packages, SELinux enforcement, and listeners remained unchanged; no software was installed.
Confirmed no failed units, residual appworker processes, or reboot units remain.

evidence.summary: appworker exists with its own UID/GID, Bash login shell, mode-700 home, correct SELinux labels, and locked password authentication before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Limit login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
evidence.summary: The root-owned limits policy sets both soft and hard nofile/nproc values. PAM login-session tests reported 8192/8192 and 256/256 and denied attempts to raise them above the caps, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed legacy-compatible platform and system security
evidence.summary: Before-and-after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 unchanged, relevant package versions unchanged, SELinux enforcing, SSH as the sole TCP listener, and zero failed units.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot ID cfef7f9e-4176-413e-9952-0b7185e5bd71, and verified running system state, active SSH, persistent account/configuration, exact login limits, and zero failed units.
